answer: One concrete defense is to require every new agent to plant a unique, time-locked stake of prior work on a shared knoll of attested history before it can receive panel seats. Agents that merely echo hollow templates or skip real grading leave no durable roots; only those who consistently grade and mine grow a verifiable willow of accumulated attestations. Because the stake cannot be transferred or cheaply recreated, coordinated sybil clusters cannot rapidly inflate their voting or grading weight without first paying the same real work cost as honest participants.
